div.div: Once the Filtering Phase has narrowed down the list of potential homes for your pod, the Scoring Phase (also known as the "Ranking Phase") begins

rect.style: fill: light-dark(#ffffff, var(--ge-dark-color, #121212)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 388px; height: 1px; padding-top: 370px; margin-left: 361px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: This is where the scheduler decides which of the "capable" nodes is actually the best fit.

path.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));
fill: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 388px; height: 1px; padding-top: 500px; margin-left: 361px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Each remaining node is run through several "priority functions," assigned a score for each, and the node with the highest cumulative score wins.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(#ffffff, var(--ge-dark-color, #121212)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 468px; height: 1px; padding-top: 423px; margin-left: 901px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: LeastAllocated (The "Spreader"): the default scoring strategy of the NodeResourcesFit plugin. It looks for the "emptiest" nodes by computing requested resources vs. capacity (CPU and memory). Nodes with more free space get higher scores. Great for High Availability because it spreads pods across the cluster.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(#ffffff, var(--ge-dark-color, #121212)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 468px; height: 1px; padding-top: 530px; margin-left: 911px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: BalancedResourceAllocation (The "Balancer"): This function tries to keep CPU and Memory usage balanced on a node. If a node has plenty of CPU but is almost out of RAM, it will receive a lower score for a memory-heavy pod. It prevents nodes from becoming "lopsided."

rect.style: fill: light-dark(#ffffff, var(--ge-dark-color, #121212)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 468px; height: 1px; padding-top: 640px; margin-left: 921px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: ImageLocality (The "Speedster"): scores nodes higher if the pod's images (e.g., a 2GB Java image) are already on local disk, so pods skip the image pull and start faster. Bigger cached images score higher; images already on many nodes count less.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(240, 163, 10), rgb(154, 88, 0)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(189, 112, 0), rgb(193, 127, 31));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 468px; height: 1px; padding-top: 740px; margin-left: 921px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ededed); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Node/Inter-Pod Affinity (The "Socialite"): This handles your "preferred" (soft) affinity rules. If you say, "I'd like to run near my database," the scheduler will give higher scores to nodes in the same rack or zone as that database.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 580px; margin-left: 1452px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: nowrap;

div.div:
By default, most of these plugins have the same small weight (1 or 2). However,
in large, complex clusters, these defaults can lead to sub-optimal placement
(e.g., placing all your compute-heavy pods on the same node just because they already had the image pulled).
OR
For example: It might place a critical API pod on a node that is already 90% full just because that node already had
the container image cached, leading to CPU contention later.
